content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working on a generator control and turbine flow monitoring setup implemented on a [product_name]. I want to know if anyone has advice on showing logs on the web server or on an HMI screen—for example, displaying the time, date, and event whenever a certain signal goes high. I've tried the data logging feature, but retrieving data is difficult, and the system overwrites older entries once there are too many, even with 64GB of SD card space. Thanks in advance! [user_name]

Hello, The built-in web server in [product_name] offers similar capabilities to message texts. From what you described, it seems you want to log when a user accesses or modifies something, but this isn’t supported by the integrated web server. While you can use a datalog, entries from the datalog cannot be displayed directly in the web server. My only suggestion is to use a message text with "Acknowledge Message" enabled. On [product_name], this message remains active until someone presses the "OK" button. The same should apply when using the web server. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are limited by the logging capabilities of the integrated web server in [product_name], particularly in displaying events and logs directly on either the web server or HMI. The built-in data logging is considered inconvenient for retrieving data and cannot store many entries, regardless of available memory. There is no option to show datalog records on the web server, which makes event monitoring challenging.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to create and display detailed logs with timestamps directly on the web server or HMI, with the ability to store large volumes of log entries when enough storage is available.
